summary: Lookout station erected on Pogey Mountain in 1915 (Piscataquis County, Maine), with a telephone line added in 1916; now listed as gone.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no readable source gives a removal date or describes the site now

events.note: Station erected on Pogey Mountain, Township 4, Range 9, per the 1916 Forest Commissioner's Report as quoted on easternuslookouts.weebly.com; the entry calls it a station, not a tower
About one and a half miles of telephone line built from the Lincoln Pulp Wood Company's line to the lookout station

evidence.supports: Piscataquis County, Gone status, FFLA list
earliest record: 1916 Forest Commissioner's report, quoted on the Kemnow list
station put up on Pogey Mountain, Township 4 Range 9, listed under 1915
evidence.quote: 1915: "Therefore erected a station on Pogey Mt. on T. 4, R. 9, which overlooks more territory and is more satisfactory." (1916 Forest Commissioner's Report)

evidence.supports: telephone line of one and a half miles to the station, listed under 1916
evidence.quote: I have built one and one-half miles of telephone line from the Lincoln Pulp Wood Company's line to lookout station on Pogey Mountain.

notes_for_editor: Both historical entries come from a compiled Maine list that quotes the Forest Commissioner's reports; I did not see the originals. The list calls the 1915 site a station, while the FFLA list calls it a tower. A Maine FFLA Facebook group snippet (facebook.com/groups/470396248872986/posts/882574660988474/) mentions a wooden tower on 'South Pogy mountain' in T4 R9 inside Baxter State Park, built 1916; it would not open here, so it is not used. Check whether that is this site, since the FFLA coordinates (46.02995, -68.94135) are unverified against the township. No access, height, design or staffing sources were found, so the story is short. The 1915 and 1916 dates are the list's year labels; the quoted text gives no year, so the story attributes the dates to the list.
